en: The Sūtra on the Ratnaśikhara Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha for the Elimination of All Calamities and Obstacles,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Dafu, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
Translated by the Imperial Subject Dharma-bhadra, the Great Master Mingjiao, by imperial decree: At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying,
"There is a dhāraṇī named Ratna-śikhara (Jewel-Crest),
which can bring great benefit to sentient beings."
It can extinguish the extremely heavy karmic offenses of sentient beings.
Ānanda, in the past, when Śakra fought with the asuras, Śakra,
the Lord of Devas, was defeated and fled in immeasurable fear.
Thereupon, he came swiftly to where the Buddha was and addressed me with piteous words:
"World-Honored One, in your great compassion, I pray that you will look upon me with pity."
"I am terrified of the asuras and cannot remain at ease.
I only pray that you, out of great compassion, will grant me peace and security.
Ānanda, having heard these words from Śakra, I...
He then addressed him, saying: "Do not fear; I shall grant you protection.
O Lord of Devas, in a past kalpa, there was a buddha-world named Avalokita."
In that land there is a Buddha named Avalokiteśvara Tathāgata.
That Buddha bestowed upon me the Ratna-śikhara Dhāraṇī;
this dhāraṇī has been spoken with one voice by one koṭi of Buddhas.
Possessing great majestic power, it is capable of bestowing auspiciousness.
Furthermore, if there are those who copy, wear upon their heads, read, recite, accept, and uphold it,
I know that such persons shall extinguish all sins and increase immeasurable merit.
It shall constantly protect you yourself and enable you to benefit others.
O Lord of Devas, you should always keep this in mind, transcribe it, and wear it upon your head;
thus, all that you undertake will accord with your wishes.
This King of Dhāraṇīs is also named Paritrāṇa;
it can bestow the most supreme and wholesome benefit upon sentient beings.
That asura should now naturally cease his mind [of hostility].
If they come to engage in battle and are subsequently defeated and subdued,
I shall then recite for them the Ratnaśikhara Dhāraṇī, saying: *Namaḥ buddhāya | Namaḥ dharmāya* | *Namaḥ saṃghāya*.
Namaḥ saṃghāya. Namaḥ sabhātanāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānām. Sarvavāgasaṃghanāṃ. Sarvabuddhabodhisattvanamaskṛtānām. Tadyathā.
He recites: Oṃ jaya-garī mudrā-raṇi pattramukta sarvam-āgala-dharāja jīmūte nana-laṅgara-viśe.

When Śakra, Lord of the Devas, had obtained this dhāraṇī, he...
Rejoicing, receive it upon your heads, remember it, and uphold it;
you shall always dwell in peace and happiness together with your retinue.
Ānanda, the power of this dhāraṇī is vast and great.
Not only does it subdue the Asura King,
but it also subdues all others, including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas,
garuḍas, kiṃnaras, as well as bhūtas, vetālas, and so forth.
Those who seek to harass and disturb sentient beings shall be unable to cause harm, as they are protected by the power of this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, it can eliminate famine, epidemics, poisons, and untimely deaths.
In dreams and sleep, inauspicious signs appear and evil māras are struck with terror.
Furthermore, there may be those who seek wealth and treasures,
or who seek offspring.
Those who uphold and recite this dhāraṇī shall all obtain immeasurable wealth according to their wishes and an increase in their retinue.
Ānanda, the merit of this dhāraṇī is exceptionally sublime.
If I were to explain it in full, it would be inexhaustible. At that time,
having heard the Buddha speak this dhāraṇī, Ānanda received and upheld it with a sincere mind,
prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
The Sūtra on the Ratnaśikhara Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha for Eliminating All Calamities and Obstacles.
